create.name: Tosha Silver
create.bio:
Tosha Silver is an American writer and teacher whose work centres on one idea: inviting the Divine to lead daily life instead of trying to manage every outcome by force of will. She studied English literature at Yale, and along the way was drawn to yogic philosophy and devotional practice. For many years she worked as an astrologer and gave tens of thousands of readings, before setting that work aside in 2012 to concentrate on writing and teaching.

She is best known for Outrageous Openness and Change Me Prayers, books of short stories, prayers and reflections on surrender, and she later wrote It's Not Your Money, on treating money as something offered to the Divine. Her tone is light and informal, and she avoids spiritual jargon where she can. Her main teaching home is an online membership, the Living Outrageous Openness Forum, which meets weekly on Zoom for a talk with questions, keeps recordings for those who cannot attend live, and has a members' discussion group. She also runs occasional short online courses, some drawing on astrology and on goddess figures such as Kali.

books.title: Outrageous Openness: Letting the Divine Take the Lead
books.author: Tosha Silver
books.description: Her first book, a collection of brief stories and reflections about handing everyday worries to a loving higher power and watching what follows. It is written in a playful voice and is meant to be dipped into.

books.title: Change Me Prayers: The Hidden Power of Spiritual Surrender
books.author: Tosha Silver
books.description: A follow-up to Outrageous Openness built around short prayers that ask to be changed from within rather than for circumstances to change. Each prayer comes with stories about work, relationships, money and self-worth.

courses.title: Living Outrageous Openness Forum
courses.description: An ongoing online membership with a weekly Zoom talk and question session led by Tosha, recorded for anyone who cannot join live. Members also get a private discussion group and discounts on her recorded classes.
